concerns.text: Task T003 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it reads the output of T002 (`mobius_array.npy`) and writes a new file. This creates a producer‑consumer dependency, so T003 cannot safely run in parallel with other tasks that might access the same data.
Task T005 is marked `[P]` yet it depends on both `window_index.csv` (produced by T004) and the Möbius array files (produced by T002/T003). It therefore cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T006 is marked `[P]` but consumes `window_index.csv` and the Möbius data generated earlier. It must run after those producers and cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T007 is marked `[P]` while it cross‑validates results from T006. It reads `autocorrelation_raw.csv` produced by T006, creating a consumer‑before‑producer risk if run in parallel.

Task T008 is marked `[P]` yet it requires the null distribution built from data produced by T006 and T007, and also writes to `autocorrelation_stats.csv` which is later consumed by T009. It is not parallel‑safe.
Task T009 is marked `[P]` but reads the CSV generated by T008 and writes back to the same file. This read‑modify‑write pattern is not safe for parallel execution.
Task T010 is marked `[P]` while it depends on the permutation pipeline (T008) and writes new JSON artifacts. Parallel execution could conflict with tasks that also read/write these artifacts.
Task T011 is marked `[P]` but re‑runs the permutation engine on variants of the data produced by T008, creating a dependency that precludes safe parallelism.
Task T012 is marked `[P]` yet it consumes `autocorrelation_stats.csv` (produced by T009) and the PNG outputs from earlier stages. It cannot be parallel‑safe.
Task T014 is marked `[P]` but writes `research.md` that references many artifacts produced by earlier tasks. It must run after those producers and is not parallel‑safe.

Task T001 is tagged `[US‑1]` but its output (`quickstart.md`) is not referenced by any functional requirement or user story, making it an orphan within the US‑1 group and breaking the independently‑shippable unit principle.
